method: Per-product comparison of lesson subject, mechanism, transaction, failure, evidence, remediation, question and diagram topology against 357 actual published lesson fingerprints. Candidate-only anti-repeat records were also reviewed separately. Each selection includes an explicit closest-prior comparison and a manual mechanism distinction.

candidates.lesson_subject: Explicit web proxy isolation: PAC delivery, proxy-policy matching, and FortiIsolator handoff
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Explicit proxy listener accepts browser-directed HTTP/HTTPS or PAC-selected traffic; proxy policy action isolate forwards selected sessions to a configured FortiIsolator server and logs isolate separately from accept; PAC file is served by FortiGate and must retain its custom certificate trust chain for HTTPS download.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Browser retrieves PAC -> FindProxyForURL selects PROXY or DIRECT -> client connects to explicit proxy listener -> proxy policy matches identity/destination/service -> accept policy forwards normally or isolate action hands request to isolator server -> FortiGate logs policy action; PAC delivery and proxy session are separate transactions.
candidates.failure_class: PAC content lost or unreachable after VDOM lifecycle operation; PAC download fails 404; browser bypasses proxy or reaches proxy but policy does not isolate; HTTPS PAC fetch rejected due to untrusted server certificate.
candidates.evidence_pattern: `get web-proxy explicit` and `show web-proxy explicit` prove PAC server/data state; HTTPS GET and certificate chain prove PAC delivery; proxy-policy logs with action=isolate prove isolator selection, not that the remote rendering container is healthy; session/traffic logs prove the proxy data path.
candidates.remediation_path: Validate the PAC URI, PAC content and VDOM context; after VDOM deletion verify root VDOM PAC content; restore empty PAC data; use a trusted custom server certificate for HTTPS PAC; verify proxy feature visibility/listener and explicit/transparent proxy policy order; validate isolator FQDN/IP, port and server reachability.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Browser can fetch PAC but suspicious browsing is not isolated; distinguish PAC selection, proxy listener, policy action, and isolator server reachability.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client browser -> HTTPS PAC service -> proxy listener -> ordered proxy-policy decision -> normal egress or FortiIsolator branch; side annotation for per-VDOM PAC storage and certificate trust.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 workflow sessions: concurrent change sets, selective approval, and conflict merge
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 workflow mode attaches independent working sessions to administrators inside one ADOM; ADOM-wide lock is no longer required; submitted sessions can be approved in any order; the approval engine detects stale-object conflicts and exposes mergeable versus conflicting changes.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin opens session -> modifies ADOM policy/object working copy -> saves/submits -> approval group reviews diff -> any session can be approved first -> accepted delta is committed to ADOM -> later overlapping session is compared against current ADOM state -> conflict view marks changed/deleted objects -> merge nonconflicting delta or repair/resubmit.
candidates.failure_class: Concurrent policy changes conflict because one session edits an object another deletes/changes; user assumes submission order equals approval order or believes workflow sessions permit device install before approval.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Session list status Waiting Approval proves submitted workflow state; View Diff proves a session's proposed delta; conflict view red/green markings prove object-level conflict classification; ADOM state after approval proves committed change; it does not prove installation to managed FortiGates, because approval updates ADOM and installation is a separate action.
candidates.remediation_path: Use one named session per logical change; review diffs before submission; inspect conflict markers; merge only nonconflicting changes; rebase/repair the session against current ADOM state and resubmit; schedule device installation separately after approval.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Two admins submit independent sessions; the later-approved session deletes a policy the earlier session edited; choose conflict-resolution semantics and distinguish ADOM approval from device installation.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two admin swimlanes with Session A and Session B converging on approval queue; Session B commit precedes A, conflict detector branches into merge-safe green and conflicting red deltas, then repair/resubmit.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 playbook execution: connector tasks, dry-run replay, node debugging, and partial reruns
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A playbook consists of a trigger plus linked connector tasks whose dependencies determine execution order; 8.0 editor adds step debugging, replay with alternate input, partial restart from a selected task, Branch/Wait/Compare/Switch control and Jinja conditions/loops.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Trigger fires (incident, schedule, or on-demand) -> task receives trigger/prior-task JSON inputs -> connector action runs -> output becomes downstream input -> branch/control/loop evaluates -> job status and task outputs/errors persist; dry run uses mock data which is cleared when saving/leaving editor.
candidates.failure_class: Playbook stops or produces incorrect downstream action because connector is inactive, task input schema is wrong, prior task output differs from assumed JSON, or branch/loop condition routes incorrectly.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Playbook Tasks dialog exposes job ID, trigger, timestamps and status; per-node input/output and step-debug result localize the failing contract; inactive connector appears grayed; dry-run output validates mapping but does not prove production connector credentials/permissions or external API availability.
candidates.remediation_path: Validate connector activation and credentials; replay with representative mock data; inspect each node's JSON input/output; test the failing task alone; use partial rerun from the corrected node; add explicit branch/compare/wait conditions and verify downstream tasks against the actual output schema.
candidates.question_fingerprint: An incident playbook fails only at the third connector task after a schema change; identify which editor feature proves the prior task output and safely reruns from the failed node.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Trigger -> Task 1 -> Branch/Compare -> Task 2 -> Wait -> Task 3; side loop for dry-run input/output inspection and partial restart at Task 3.

candidates.lesson_subject: LLDP-MED network-policy advertisement for voice VLAN, L2 priority, DSCP and endpoint power
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch LLDP-MED extends LLDP with network-policy, location, inventory and PoE power TLVs; an LLDP profile controls TLVs and MED network-policy entries per port; VLAN-bound policy values are advertised only when that VLAN is assigned to the interface.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable global LLDP -> create LLDP profile and MED network-policy TLVs -> assign profile to edge port -> ensure voice VLAN is allowed/native as required -> switch multicasts LLDP frames -> phone learns VLAN, L2 priority and DSCP -> phone tags voice frames accordingly.
candidates.failure_class: Phone remains in data VLAN or marks voice traffic incorrectly because LLDP profile is absent, LLDP disabled, VLAN not assigned to port, or MED TLV is not enabled; operator expects LLDP to configure a switch port's VLAN without the VLAN actually existing.
candidates.evidence_pattern: `show switch lldp profile` proves profile TLV content; `get switch lldp neighbors-detail`/LLDP details prove peer received/sent TLVs; port VLAN membership proves local forwarding domain; phone VLAN and packet capture prove endpoint behavior; LLDP neighbor presence alone does not prove a MED network-policy TLV was advertised.
candidates.remediation_path: Create profile with med-network-policy and inventory-management TLVs; assign profile to the intended physical port; configure voice VLAN and ensure VLAN membership; enable LLDP; validate the received policy on the phone and tagged frames; check PoE budget separately from MED power TLV.
candidates.question_fingerprint: IP phone discovers the switch but remains untagged on data VLAN; identify the missing MED network-policy/VLAN membership relationship rather than assuming basic LLDP neighbor discovery is sufficient.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch edge port with LLDP-MED profile advertises VLAN 400/priority 5/DSCP 46 and PoE TLVs to IP phone; phone sends tagged voice traffic while attached PC uses data VLAN.

candidates.lesson_subject: RADIUS VLAN name tags and round-robin VLAN pools on a single enterprise SSID
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise RADIUS Access-Accept can return Tunnel-Type=VLAN, Tunnel-Medium-Type=IEEE-802 and Tunnel-Private-Group-ID; the last attribute may identify a VLAN ID, interface name, or a configured vlan-name key. A vlan-name key can map to up to eight VLAN IDs selected round-robin.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client associates to one bridge-mode SSID -> EAP/RADIUS authentication -> Access-Accept returns VLAN name tag -> FortiGate wireless controller resolves the tag through the VAP vlan-name table -> selects one mapped VLAN ID -> client traffic is bridged/tagged into that VLAN -> DHCP and firewall policy apply to the selected VLAN interface.
candidates.failure_class: Authentication succeeds but client lands on default or wrong VLAN because Tunnel-Private-Group-ID does not exactly match a VLAN ID/interface name/name-tag key, the dynamic-vlan setting is off, or selected VLAN is absent from the bridge path.
candidates.evidence_pattern: RADIUS Access-Accept attributes prove the server returned the expected tag; VAP `show` proves dynamic-vlan and vlan-name mappings; wireless client table proves assigned VLAN; DHCP lease and switch trunk capture prove end-to-end VLAN reachability; successful EAP alone does not prove VLAN assignment.
candidates.remediation_path: Align RADIUS attribute values and case-sensitive name-tag keys; enable dynamic-vlan on the VAP; define VLAN ID pool (maximum eight per name); ensure switch trunks and FortiGate VLAN interfaces/DHCP/policies exist; verify round-robin distribution across new authentications.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Users authenticate on one SSID but only some receive the intended subnet; identify the name-tag pool mapping and distinguish authentication success from VLAN resolution and DHCP reachability.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Single bridge-mode SSID -> RADIUS Access-Accept with `data` name tag -> VAP vlan-name table -> round-robin VLAN100/200/300 pool -> DHCP/policy paths.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiNAC Local RADIUS Server as the 802.1X EAP termination point
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC Local RADIUS Server terminates 802.1X EAP locally instead of proxying EAP to an external RADIUS server; supports selected EAP methods, TLS/cipher profile, endpoint trust certificates, OCSP for EAP-TLS, Winbind for MSCHAPv2 and RADIUS attribute groups; accounting is not provided by Local RADIUS.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Supplicant sends EAPOL -> switch/AP relays RADIUS Access-Request to FortiNAC local RADIUS port -> EAP method negotiates with FortiNAC -> FortiNAC validates certificate/OCSP or directory/local user -> Access-Accept with attribute group drives VLAN/role -> accounting, if required, is separately proxied to external RADIUS.
candidates.failure_class: EAP-TLS fails due to missing/untrusted root CA or absent OCSP URL; MSCHAPv2 fails because Winbind/domain membership is wrong; Local and Proxy services collide on authentication port; operator expects Local RADIUS to provide accounting.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Local RADIUS service log shows EAP negotiation and request/response attributes; server log/system journal shows service state; certificate chain/OCSP response prove trust and revocation status; Access-Accept attributes prove policy response; successful Access-Accept does not prove accounting was forwarded.
candidates.remediation_path: Install server certificate and Endpoint Trust CA; configure supported EAP types and matching TLS protocols/ciphers; configure Winbind for AD MSCHAPv2; enable OCSP only when client certificates contain responder URL; use a distinct authentication port from proxy service; configure external accounting proxy if accounting is needed.
candidates.question_fingerprint: 802.1X EAP-TLS succeeds on external RADIUS but fails after moving termination to FortiNAC; diagnose Endpoint Trust/OCSP and account for the separate accounting limitation.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Supplicant -> access switch/AP -> FortiNAC Local RADIUS EAP state machine -> certificate/OCSP or Winbind/local identity -> Access-Accept attributes -> VLAN/role; separate accounting proxy path.

candidates.lesson_subject: TEAP chained user-and-machine authentication with Microsoft Entra ID in FortiNAC-F 7.6.3
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: TEAP establishes a protected EAP tunnel and carries inner authentication methods; FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 supports multiple inner methods, including user and computer authentication, and can use an Entra ID service connector/domain mapping as the authentication source for RADIUS virtual servers.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Windows supplicant starts EAP-TEAP -> FortiNAC-F RADIUS virtual server negotiates outer TLS tunnel -> TEAP inner method authenticates user and/or computer in configured order -> Entra ID service connector resolves identity -> policy/group mapping returns authorization -> switch port applies 802.1X result; HA requires consistent connector and virtual-server configuration.
candidates.failure_class: TEAP tunnel establishes but inner identity fails because primary/secondary auth type differs from Windows profile, Entra connector/domain mapping is missing, or TLS trust/certificate is incomplete; computer authentication is omitted and device posture/authorization differs from expectation.
candidates.evidence_pattern: RADIUS virtual-server supported EAP list proves TEAP enabled; TEAP negotiation log shows outer tunnel and inner method stage; Entra connector test proves API/credential path; Windows EAP event log identifies client-side method mismatch; Access-Accept proves final authorization but not that both user and machine identities were checked unless both inner stages appear.
candidates.remediation_path: Create Entra service connector and domain mapping; attach it to the RADIUS virtual server; enable TLS and TEAP; set primary/secondary inner auth types to match the intended user/computer sequence; configure Windows EAP-TEAP; validate CA trust, connector credentials, and policy mapping.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Windows clients complete outer TEAP TLS but receive Access-Reject after machine authentication; identify the mismatch between FortiNAC-F TEAP inner-method order and the Windows supplicant profile.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Windows supplicant -> EAP-TEAP outer TLS tunnel -> FortiNAC-F virtual server -> inner user auth + inner computer auth -> Entra ID service connector -> policy mapping -> switch port authorization.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator RADIUS proxy transparency and Message-Authenticator enforcement
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Remote RADIUS server profile can use Proxy as preferred authentication method to preserve the authentication method/credential exchange unchanged; realm preservation can retain the qualified username; when FAC is the RADIUS client it sends Message-Authenticator, and an optional response requirement rejects upstream responses that omit it.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: NAS sends Access-Request to FAC -> FAC selects remote RADIUS profile and forwards original auth method/attributes -> upstream RADIUS validates and returns Access-Accept/Reject -> FAC validates response integrity attribute if required -> FAC returns result to NAS; optional secondary server is used for redundancy.
candidates.failure_class: Proxy authentication fails because remote server does not support the original EAP/auth method, realm is stripped or rewritten, response lacks required Message-Authenticator, or timeout is too long and stalls request throughput.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Remote RADIUS server profile shows Preferred auth method=Proxy, timeout, realm option and secondary server; packet capture shows request/response attributes and Message-Authenticator; FAC RADIUS debug identifies upstream timeout/reject; an Access-Accept without integrity validation does not prove response policy is enforced.
candidates.remediation_path: Choose Proxy only when upstream supports the original method; preserve realm when hierarchical proxy routing needs it; enable response Message-Authenticator requirement only after confirming upstream compatibility; configure realistic timeout and secondary server; verify request/response packet attributes on both legs.
candidates.question_fingerprint: FAC relays Access-Requests but upstream accepts only some clients after security hardening; distinguish method transparency, realm preservation and Message-Authenticator response enforcement.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: NAS -> FortiAuthenticator RADIUS proxy -> primary/secondary upstream RADIUS; show original auth method and realm passing through, with Message-Authenticator validation at FAC response boundary.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 approved-secret request revocation and immediate session termination
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 adds Revoke Approval for already-approved secret access requests; revocation is permitted regardless of approval tier and even after launch; if a session is active it is terminated immediately and the request resets to require approval/denial again. This differs from legacy per-tier Revoke button availability.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Requester submits secret access request -> approval profile routes through one or more tiers -> approval is granted -> requester launches secret -> approver selects Revoke Approval on approved request -> FortiPAM invalidates authorization and terminates active session -> request returns to pending decision state.
candidates.failure_class: Approver cannot revoke after request is fully approved or session has launched because operator uses old tier-specific Revoke semantics or has insufficient visibility; access remains active when approval revocation is not invoked.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Secrets > Approvals shows request state and Revoke Approval action; Active Sessions shows launched session and termination; request status reset proves reapproval required; browser/session termination proves active access ended, not that target credentials were rotated.
candidates.remediation_path: Upgrade/use FortiPAM 1.9+; configure approval profile and approver permissions; use Revoke Approval on the approved request; verify active session termination and request reset; rotate target credential separately if compromise is suspected.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A vendor has already launched a secret session after multi-tier approval; select the 1.9 action that immediately terminates the active session and resets approval.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Requester -> approval tiers -> approved request -> launched secret session; approver revocation branch invalidates request, sends terminate to active session, and returns request to Waiting Approval.

candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Business Services: CMDB membership, incident impact tagging, and service-centric triage
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A Business Service is a logical collection of devices and applications representing a business function; membership can be manual or generated by Dynamic CMDB Groups; FortiSIEM tags incidents with impacted Business Services and presents incident-centric dashboards and drilldowns.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Discover/normalize devices and applications into CMDB -> create Business Service with explicit members or dynamic filter -> event correlation creates incident against CMDB entities -> FortiSIEM resolves entity membership to Business Service -> incident/dashboard shows service impact -> analyst drills into device/application performance, availability and related incidents.
candidates.failure_class: Incident is present but business-service dashboard does not show impact because affected CMDB entity is missing, duplicated, stale, or excluded by service filter; overly broad membership causes unrelated incidents to appear critical.
candidates.evidence_pattern: CMDB entity identity and Business Service membership prove relationship; incident detail's impacted-service tag proves correlation; service dashboard drilldown shows availability/performance/incident status; service membership alone does not prove the application dependency is current or causal.
candidates.remediation_path: Normalize entity identifiers and discovery credentials; verify device and application objects in CMDB; inspect Business Service member/filter selections; use Dynamic CMDB Group criteria carefully; validate incident impact tagging against a known test incident and review stale/duplicate entities.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A database outage triggers a host incident but the payments Business Service dashboard remains green; identify the missing CMDB application/device membership or dynamic group filter.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: CMDB device/application entities -> manual or dynamic Business Service membership -> event correlation incident -> impacted-service tag -> service dashboard and drilldown.

candidates.lesson_subject: Agentless ZTNA for HTTPS private applications: proxy SSO, SPA service connection, and browser identity
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Agentless ZTNA exposes HTTPS private web apps through FortiSASE proxy and SSO with a Secure Private Access service connection; no endpoint FortiClient agent or endpoint ZTNA certificate is required, but the application must sit behind a FortiGate SPA hub and subscription/features must be licensed/configured.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Browser user authenticates to FortiSASE proxy SSO -> agentless ZTNA policy maps user to private HTTPS application -> FortiSASE traverses SPA/BGP overlay to FortiGate hub -> FortiGate access proxy forwards to private web app -> per-session user authentication/authorization is enforced -> response returns through proxy.
candidates.failure_class: User authenticates to proxy but private app is unreachable because SPA overlay/BGP, hub proxy, HTTPS app certificate, policy, subscription, or proxy SSO prerequisite is missing; operator mistakenly expects agentless mode to provide endpoint posture attributes.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Feature entitlement and Proxy/Proxy SSO/SPA configuration prove prerequisites; SPA BGP/overlay route proves private path; FortiGate ZTNA access-proxy logs prove hub policy decision; proxy SSO logs prove user identity; successful portal login alone does not prove app path or application authorization.
candidates.remediation_path: Confirm Advanced/Comprehensive remote-user subscription; enable Proxy and Proxy SSO; establish SPA BGP overlay to FortiGate hub; configure HTTPS private app and FortiGate ZTNA access proxy; map user/group policy; validate TLS chain and route; do not rely on endpoint posture tags in agentless mode.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A contractor without FortiClient can authenticate to FortiSASE but cannot reach an internal HTTPS app; identify missing SPA/FortiGate access-proxy path rather than endpoint certificate enrollment.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Browser-only user -> FortiSASE proxy SSO -> agentless ZTNA app policy -> SPA/BGP overlay -> FortiGate ZTNA access proxy -> private HTTPS app; no FortiClient endpoint agent.

candidates.lesson_subject: BGP community-to-route-tag translation for dynamic SD-WAN destination matching
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: An inbound BGP route-map matches a received standard community and sets a local route-tag on the learned prefix; a route-tag firewall address object and SD-WAN service rule then match the dynamic route set without hard-coding remote prefixes. The route-tag is local metadata, not a BGP path attribute.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Neighbor advertises prefix with BGP community -> inbound route-map matches community -> FortiGate attaches local route-tag -> route-tag address object matches installed route -> firewall policy permits traffic to SD-WAN zone -> SD-WAN service rule selects member based on tag and strategy/SLA.
candidates.failure_class: BGP route is learned but traffic matches default SD-WAN rule because route-map is attached outbound instead of inbound, community-list does not match, route-tag object is missing, or operator expects the local route-tag to be advertised to peers.
candidates.evidence_pattern: `get router info bgp network` shows received community and RouteTag; route table confirms prefix installation; route-tag address object and SD-WAN rule show tag binding; debug flow/session proves rule match; BGP community alone does not prove local route-tag was set or that the selected member is healthy.
candidates.remediation_path: Match community with inbound route-map; set-route-tag on inbound route-map; verify learned route tag; create address object of type route-tag; reference it in firewall and SD-WAN service rules; validate policy, default route, SLA and member state; never rely on route-tag in route-map-out for peer advertisement.
candidates.question_fingerprint: A branch advertises dynamic data-center prefixes with a BGP community, but SD-WAN uses the default WAN; identify inbound community-to-local-route-tag mapping and the route-tag address object.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote BGP neighbor community -> FortiGate inbound community-list/route-map -> local route tag -> route-tag address object -> SD-WAN service rule -> selected WAN member.
